title: decade-channel re-declares the server's message types and the two have drifted
body:
`channel.rs` declares `Hello`, `Focus`, `Status`, `AgentState` (Idle, Working, Done, Attention, with `Ord`) and `PaneInfo`. `decade-channel/src/lib.rs` declares `AgentState` again in the order Attention, Done, Working, Idle and without `Ord`, and `Pane`. decade does not depend on decade-channel. The server builds `welcome` with `json!` and the client reads it by indexing a `Value`, `welcome["version"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0)`. The client builds `hello`, `focus` and `status` through a 40-line `object()` helper that inserts into a `Map`, though it already derives serde for `Pane` and `code::Show`. Nothing in this repository reads the client's `VERSION` or `welcome.version`; decade-apps may.

## Proposal

decade-channel exports derived `Hello`, `Focus`, `Status`, `Welcome`, `Error`, `Pane` and `AgentState` in the server's order. decade takes it as a path dependency and `channel.rs` uses those types. A `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` enum writes the one-key messages with no hand-built maps.

## Cost

A minor bump of `decade-channel` under the versioning rule in `CLAUDE.md`. Check decade-apps for uses of the `AgentState` order and of `VERSION` first.
close_reason: Landed in 49896bf. `decade-channel` declares the message types and `AgentState` in the server order, and `decade` imports them. The version stays at 0.1.0 because `decade-channel` has never been released.
